source.author: verg
source.text: Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_original: 'Principio caelum ac terras camposque liquentis / lucentemque globum Lunae Titaniaque astra / spiritus intus alit, totamque infusa per artus / mens agitat molem et magno se corpore miscet.
source.text_english: First, within the heavens, the lands, the watery plains, the shining orb of the Moon, and the Titanian stars, a spirit nourishes all things from within; poured through its limbs, mind stirs the whole mass and mingles itself with the great body.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: quod si mundum spiritus intus alit to tamque infusa per artus mens molem et magno se corpore , apparet testimonio poetae unum esse mundi habitatorem deum, siquidem corpus omne nisi ab una mente incoli regique non potest.
reuse.text_original: quod si mundum spiritus intus alit to tamque infusa per artus mens molem et magno se corpore , apparet testimonio poetae unum esse mundi habitatorem deum, siquidem corpus omne nisi ab una mente incoli regique non potest.
reuse.text_english: But if the spirit within nourishes the world, and if a mind so deeply infused through the limbs and the mass itself and through the great body, it is clear, by the poet’s testimony, that God is the single inhabitant of the world, since no body whatever can be inhabited and governed except by one mind.
